result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's plan follows the right order: audit usage, put the existing values behind tokens without changing anything visible, merge the near-duplicates, then rework components. It also leaves room for card and panel to stay different and keeps a separate elevation for the modal. B combines defining tokens and snapping values onto them in one step, wrongly calls that change mostly invisible, and folds card, panel and modal into one surface with a small or medium shadow, which flattens the modal's intentional elevation. B is more explicit about only having seen one excerpt, but it never names the shadow differences as a cause. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B covers all the causes, including shadows that differ slightly, which A leaves out of its diagnosis. B's order is better justified: audit usage, add tokens without changing visuals, consolidate, then normalize components, and it says that merging near-duplicates will cause visible shifts. A calls snapping values to tokens 'mostly invisible' and folds the modal into the card and panel surface without arguing for it, though A is a little tighter; B's mention of a 'design-system-builder skill' is an odd unsupported aside.
